name: Ancient world trivia (hard)
description: 50 hard questions about prehistory and the early civilizations: Mesopotamia, Egypt, the Indus, China, the Americas. Written by Claude from cited web pages; every question names its page. Checked by a second model pass; the questions it flagged were corrected or left out.

source.name: Web pages cited on each question

items.question: According to the Sumerian king list, Gilgamesh of Uruk reigned after which event?
items.explain: Britannica notes that the Sumerian king list mentions Gilgamesh of Uruk as reigning after the Flood. The historical Gilgamesh probably ruled in the first half of the 3rd millennium BCE.

items.question: The fullest surviving text of the Gilgamesh epic comes from tablets found at Nineveh in the library of which Assyrian king?
items.explain: The fullest extant text is on 12 incomplete Akkadian tablets from the library of Ashurbanipal, who reigned 668–627 BCE.

items.question: Which scribe is credited with composing the most complete Akkadian version of the Epic of Gilgamesh in the Middle Babylonian period?
items.explain: The most complete account of Gilgamesh's adventures was composed in Akkadian by a scribe named Sîn-lēqi-unninni.

items.question: In the Gilgamesh epic, which creature seizes the plant Gilgamesh obtained on his quest, so that he returns to Uruk unhappy?
items.explain: After Gilgamesh obtained the plant, a serpent seized it and he returned to Uruk without it.

items.question: Which son of Ur-Nammu do some scholars credit with writing the law code that bears his father's name?
items.explain: Some scholars have attributed the Code of Ur-Nammu to his son Shulgi, although the prologue credits Ur-Nammu.

items.question: Unlike the later 'eye for an eye' approach of Babylonian law, how did the Code of Ur-Nammu mostly punish bodily injury?
answers: With forced labour on temple lands
With public flogging in the city
With banishment from the home city
items.explain: The code instituted monetary compensation for bodily damage rather than later lex talionis, though capital crimes like murder and robbery were still punished by death.

source.title: The Ur-Nammu Law Code, the Oldest Known Legal Code

items.question: The first copy of the Code of Ur-Nammu, found in two fragments and translated by Samuel Kramer in 1952, came from which Sumerian city?
items.explain: The first copy was found in two fragments at Nippur and translated by Kramer in 1952. Later tablets from Ur and Sippar filled in more of the text.

source.title: The Ur-Nammu Law Code, the Oldest Known Legal Code

items.question: Which king carried off the stele bearing Hammurabi's laws to Susa as plunder in the 12th century BCE?
items.explain: The Louvre stele was discovered at Susa, where the Elamite king Shutruk-Nahhunte had taken it as plunder.

source.title: The Code of Hammurabi, Discovered in Khuzestan, Iran

items.question: The Louvre's Law Code of Hammurabi is described as a set of how many rules or laws?
items.explain: The Law Code of Hammurabi refers to a set of 282 rules enacted by the Babylonian king who reigned 1792–1750 BCE.

items.question: According to the Sumerian king list, Sargon of Akkad began his career as cupbearer to which king?
items.explain: The Sumerian King List says Sargon was a cupbearer to King Ur-Zababa of Kish before he rose to power.

source.title: Sargon of Akkad facts for kids

items.question: Which grandson of Sargon of Akkad ruled when the Akkadian Empire reached its greatest height?
items.explain: Sargon's sons ruled well, but the empire's height came under his grandson Naram-Sin.

source.title: Sargon of Akkad: From Gardener to King of the Four Corners of the World

items.question: What were the earliest pictographic tablets from Uruk mainly records of?
items.explain: The earliest Sumerian tablets from Uruk are mainly inventories, with drawings of commodities, numerals and personal names.

items.question: What kind of text is the latest firmly datable cuneiform tablet, written at Uruk in AD 79/80?
items.explain: Cuneiform lasted about three millennia, and the latest firmly datable tablet is an astronomical almanac from Uruk dated AD 79/80.

items.question: When Göbekli Tepe was first investigated in the 1960s, what was it dismissed as?
items.explain: Britannica notes that early investigators in the 1960s dismissed the Neolithic site as a medieval cemetery.

items.question: Which archaeologist was the original excavator of Göbekli Tepe and interpreted it as a sanctuary used by hunter-gatherers?
items.explain: Klaus Schmidt, the site's original excavator, interpreted it as a religious sanctuary established and visited by hunter-gatherers.

source.title: Echo from the Past: How Göbekli Tepe is Reshaping Our Understanding of the Neolithic

items.question: Roughly how many years does Göbekli Tepe predate Stonehenge, according to Britannica?
items.explain: Britannica says Göbekli Tepe predates Stonehenge by some 6,000 years.

items.question: What does the Turkish name Göbekli Tepe mean?
items.explain: Göbekli Tepe means 'Potbelly Hill' in Turkish, a name that reflects the shape of the mound.

items.question: The Rosetta Stone carries a royal decree of 196 BCE issued in honour of which ruler?
items.explain: Scholars deduced from the Greek text that it was a 196 BCE decree honouring the boy king Ptolemy V Epiphanes on the first anniversary of his coronation.

source.title: Science history: Rosetta stone is deciphered, opening a window into ancient Egyptian civilization — Sept. 27, 1822

items.question: Which French officer recognised the significance of the Rosetta Stone when Napoleon's forces uncovered it while building fortifications?
items.explain: Officer Pierre-François Xavier Bouchard immediately recognised the juxtaposed Greek and hieroglyphic scripts and predicted correctly that they were translations of one text.

source.title: The Rosetta Stone: Unlocking the Ancient Egyptian Language - ARCE

items.question: Champollion's fluency in which language, a descendant of ancient Egyptian, helped him decipher the hieroglyphs?
items.explain: Champollion benefited from Thomas Young's work on cartouches and from his fluency in Coptic, a language descended from ancient Egyptian.

source.title: The Rosetta Stone: Discovery and Decoding Ancient Languages

items.question: Which scholar, seventeen years older than Champollion, made major early progress on the hieroglyphic and demotic scripts and became his rival?
items.explain: Thomas Young (born 1773) was seventeen years older than Champollion (born 1790) and made incredible progress, but Champollion led the final breakthrough.

source.title: The Rosetta Stone: Unlocking the Ancient Egyptian Language - ARCE

items.question: The Rosetta Stone is a slab of which kind of stone, inscribed in Greek, hieroglyphics and demotic?
items.explain: Live Science describes the Rosetta Stone as a slab of granodiorite inscribed in three scripts.

source.title: Science history: Rosetta stone is deciphered, opening a window into ancient Egyptian civilization — Sept. 27, 1822

items.question: Which vizier of Khufu is believed by some to have been the architect of the Great Pyramid?
items.explain: Hemiunu, Khufu's vizier, is believed by some to be the architect of the Great Pyramid.

items.question: Which pharaoh was the father of Khufu, who commissioned the Great Pyramid at Giza?
items.explain: The Smithsonian notes that the Great Pyramid was commissioned by Snefru's son Khufu, also known as Cheops.

items.question: Roughly how many blocks does the Great Pyramid of Khufu contain, by Smarthistory's estimate?
items.explain: Smarthistory estimates that the Great Pyramid contains around 2,300,000 blocks, some weighing upwards of 50 tons.

items.question: What does Akhetaten, the capital Akhenaten built at modern Amarna, mean?
items.explain: Akhenaten named his new capital Akhetaten, 'The Horizon of the Aten', now known as Tell el-Amarna.

source.title: Amarna Style, Akhenaten, and Nefertiti: Egypt's Radical Revolution

items.question: In the sixth year of Akhenaten's reign, Nefertiti's name was changed to what?
items.explain: World History Encyclopedia reports that in the sixth year Nefertiti's name was changed to Nefernefruaten, meaning 'Beautiful in beauty is Aten'.

items.question: Which short-reigning pharaoh, named as Akhenaten's successor, have some scholars proposed was actually Nefertiti?
items.explain: The Berlin museum notes it is possible that Smenkhkare, named as Akhenaten's successor, was in fact Nefertiti, though inscriptions do not confirm this.

items.question: Which English archaeologist initiated and directed the original excavations at Harappa beginning in 1921?
items.explain: Britannica says Sir John Hubert Marshall initiated and directed the original excavations at Harappa from 1921.

items.question: Mohenjo-daro's builders mainly used which material for construction, reserving mud brick for fillings and mass work?
items.explain: Britannica says Mohenjo-daro employs burned brick, with mud brick reserved for fillings and mass work.

source.title: India - Indus Valley, Harappan, Bronze Age

items.question: Which domestic bird might the people of the Indus Valley civilization have been the first to raise?
items.explain: Britannica Kids says the Indus people were among the first to grow cotton and might also have been the first to raise chickens.

items.question: Besides bulls and elephants, which creature does Britannica say is especially common on carved seals from Mohenjo-daro?
items.explain: Seals from Mohenjo-daro are carved with animals such as bulls, elephants and especially unicorns, and carry Indus script inscriptions.

items.question: Before archaeologists understood their value, farmers near Anyang sold inscribed oracle bones to be ground up for what purpose?
items.explain: For centuries farmers dug up inscribed bones but sold them to apothecaries, who ground them up for Traditional Chinese Medicine.

source.title: 7 Everyday Objects From the Shang Dynasty

items.question: Which scholar discovered in 1908 that the oracle bones came from near Anyang, the site of the last Shang capital?
items.explain: In 1908 Luo Zhenyu discovered the source of the bones near Anyang and realised it was the site of the last Shang capital.

items.question: Which Shang king is traditionally credited with moving the capital to Yin, near modern Anyang, around 1350 BCE?
items.explain: Oracle bone divination dates to the middle of the Shang, probably under Pan Geng, around 1350 BCE when the capital moved to Yin.

source.title: Exploring Chinese History :: Culture :: Archaeology :: Oracle Bones

items.question: According to the historian Sima Qian, which liquid metal simulated China's great rivers in Qin Shi Huang's tomb?
items.explain: Sima Qian described the Yangtze and Yellow River being simulated in the tomb with mercury, under a ceiling decorated with constellations.

source.title: Top 10 facts about the Terracotta Warriors

items.question: The weapons found with the terra-cotta army, still sharp today, were cast from an unusual alloy of how many elements?
items.explain: Britannica notes that the swords and other weapons were cast from an unusual 13-element alloy and are still shiny and sharp.

items.question: In which direction does the buried terra-cotta army face, poised for battle?
items.explain: The army faces east, guarding the tomb from Qin Shi Huang's chief former adversaries, who had come from that direction.

items.question: Which Olmec site's colossal heads are believed to be the oldest and the most skilfully executed?
items.explain: The San Lorenzo heads are believed to be the oldest and most skilfully executed, and they were buried by about 900 BC.

items.question: Around 900 BC, which Olmec centre succeeded San Lorenzo as the civilization's main centre?
items.explain: San Lorenzo was succeeded as the main Olmec centre by La Venta in about 900 BC.

items.question: Two of the colossal heads at San Lorenzo were re-carved from what earlier monuments?
items.explain: Most colossal heads were sculpted from spherical boulders, but two from San Lorenzo were re-carved from massive stone thrones.

items.question: Which Peruvian archaeologist first identified Caral-Supe as an independent civilization and has written about it since 1994?
items.explain: Ruth Shady first identified the Norte Chico or Caral-Supe civilization as an independent civilization and has been writing about it since 1994.

items.question: Which knotted-cord recording system dates back at least to the Wari Empire and possibly to Caral in the third millennium BCE?
items.explain: The use of the quipu dates back at least to the Wari Empire (600–1000 CE) and possibly to the much earlier Caral/Norte Chico civilization.

items.question: Caral, the best-known Norte Chico site, lies in which Peruvian river valley?
items.explain: Caral is located in the Supe Valley in Barranca Province, north of Lima, which gives the civilization its alternative name Caral-Supe.

items.question: Which Norte Chico site in the Fortaleza Valley is believed to be the earliest city of that civilization, established around 3500 BC?
items.explain: Huaricanga, in the Fortaleza Valley, is described as the earliest city of the Norte Chico civilization, established around 3500 BC.

items.question: Most historians think the Maya Long Count began on a base date in which year?
items.explain: Most historians think 4 Ahau 8 Cumku, most likely 11 August 3114 BCE, was the Long Count's base date.

items.question: Combining the Maya 260-day ritual cycle with the 365-day year gives a Calendar Round of 18,980 days, equal to how many 365-day years?
items.explain: The two cycles together form a 18,980-day Calendar Round, or 52 years of 365 days.

items.question: What is the common name for the Maya 260-day ritual cycle, whose original name is unknown?
items.explain: The original name of the 260-day cycle is unknown. It is variously called the Tzolkin ('Count of Days'), divinatory calendar, ritual calendar or day calendar.

items.question: In the Early Classic Period, Tikal was an important post in a trading network established by which central Mexican city?
items.explain: Britannica says Tikal was an important post in the great trading network established in southern Mesoamerica by Teotihuacán.

items.question: Which Preclassic city is considered one of the first capital cities of the Maya civilization?
items.explain: El Mirador is considered one of the first capital cities of the Maya civilization, and it was larger than Tikal was at that time.
